[quote=montfleur;61639696][b]August 5, 2028: A Rapidly Escalating Situation[/b][/quote]
[spoiler=[b]Operation Fusilier[/b]][b]Operation Fusilier[/b]

After successfully pushing back Belgardian forces by some 30 odd kilometers, the Count of Porcéan would order his forces to momentarily halt its advance to get a better view of the strategic situation.

As had been assessed by the Other Ministry, Rosenmarkket forces were weak and dispersed, their chain of command decentralized out of necessity due to the immense damage brought on by the war in the White Straits. Thus, the speed of their advance had been largely anticipated. However, what was not anticipated was the continued capabilities of the Rosenmarkket to deploy air assets, let alone jet fighters, to counteract their invasion.

Or at least, that was what Porcéan had been meaning to report, until word would suddenly reach him of the actual destination of the jets.

In a bewildering report, the Sallacher military leadership would catch wind of what appears to have been a Rosenmarkket bombing run on Belgarde's own provincial palace, apparently undertaken by Central Forces in a desperate bid to disarm its periphery regions from any attempts at military secession. Puzzled by these circumstances, Porcéan would relay to the Regenerator Government if there had been "any significant changes" to his intended role in this invasion.

Indeed, after a brief pause in the fighting, the Count of Porcéan would receive affirmation from chief minister Odo de Baltemont himself, bluntly stating for him to do [i]"... tout ce qui vient naturellement"[/i] in order to ensure the total triumph of Sallacher objectives, to constrain the spread of communism, and to build a Montfleurois state that is beneficial to Sallacher interests.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Régence de La Rosemarche[/b]][b]Régence de La Rosemarche[/b]

With momentous backing from the better-equipped Montfleurois Army behind him, and with an expanded mandated and looser restrictions on ROE against a force that was content to fire on civilians, the Count of Porcéan would agree to "make provision for the eventual accession of these territories to an expanded Montfleur", and would order his Corps of Gendarmes to begin systematically dismantling the Rosenmarkket soviets and subsuming their duties into a singular quasi-governmental organization.

In a meeting with Rosenmarkket collaborators and dissidents, particularly community leaders that had been worst affected by the bombing runs, the Count of Porcéan would agree that the best course of action for now to fill in the power vacuum left behind by the collapsing central government was to become the government himself. 

Shortly after 8 AM, the Count of Porcéan would formally proclaim the formation of the [i]Régence de La Rosemarche[/i] ("Regency of the Rose March"), a client state setup by Sallach to administer its interests in the region. Naturally, the Count of Porcéan would be established as its first regent, while several key institutions would also be created to give the Regency some veneer of legitimacy while the rest of the invasion had been proceeding along well.

A provisional Senate of Rosemarche would be created by decree, copied directly from the functions of the Senate of Sallach. This Senate would be staffed exclusively from Sallacher military officers and Rosenmarkket collaborators, and would be given two roles. First, the Economic Department, to be headed by a chief executive, who was to deal with all civilian functions of the new state such as taxation, transport, construction, and the continued operation of public services. Second, the Judicial Department, headed by a procurator, who functioned as the supreme court of the land in the absence of functioning judiciaries.

While the Count of Porcéan had initially hoped to fully copy the Sallacher senatorial system onto the new state, "logistical realities" would force him to carry out this simplified framework, and he would quickly make appointments to the chief executive and the procuratorate later in the day before departing for the frontlines to continue Operation Fusilier.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Battle of the Gardens[/b]][b]Battle of the Gardens[/b]

Initially, Sallacher forces had intended to storm the ducal palace to force the resignation of Antoine Jacques's government. Now, it had realized that the true objective was really to save that administration and to prevent the wider region from further falling into anarchy. 

The Count of Porcéan, bolstered by Montfleurois support and having been allowed to refuel and resupply undisturbed at the captured airfields, would continue its advance deeper into Bellegarde, hoping to reach the gardens of the ducal palace and force the final and total surrender of all Rosenmarkket forces in the area. 

Char 15 tanks roared deeply across the Belgardian countryside in the long approach to the ducal palace, while Sallacher reconnaissance teams and drone squads carefully navigated the dense hedges and forestry to guide the Count of Porcéan's columns away from soviet ambush. Meanwhile, the Sallacher Air Wing had succeeded in ferrying some 500 reinforcing gendarmes to support the invasion along with artillery and extra vehicles.

Assuming all goes well, the Count of Porcéan would be optimistic about total triumph in Belgarde within the week.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=The Northern Conquests: Part 1 - The Increasing Northern Threat]
[b][u]The Increasing Northern Threat[/b][/u]
Ever since the reformation of the New Empire, many of those who did become part of the new Empire had stubbornly persisted in their rebellion to the authority of the House of Augustus. The most persistent and chaotic of them lay north of the Empires current borders, north of the old frontier lands now known as the Dukelands. There lay the following rogue states;

- Raffordshire
- Berimond
- Grockham
- Eastcaster
- Rangehill

All of whom had been a persistent nuisance to the Empire. Much of the common activities of said states have involved the murder and killing of the Empires subjects, with large bands of men heading into border regions and kidnapping, looting, raping and pillaging the settlers of the Empires frontier regions. This had prompted the usage of various internal state agencies such as Imperial Enforcement Corps (IEC) to begin major operations within the region to pacify the area. 

At first, this proved to be effective. Many rogue raiders had been captured and their activities suppressed. But, this unfortunately did not quell the issue as soon as the Smugglers Cove massacre. Smugglers Cove had been known formerly to be a haven for pirates before becoming a more civilised and established place. It is famously known to be the easternmost point of the Empires northern borders which had become notorious for cross-border smuggling due to the general lack of proper government control of the Dukelands but also due to the corruption of the local Argosi native chiefs who had ran the towns civic positions. 

This became increasingly well known to the wider populace of the Empire which eventually caught the wind of the Empires officials. It became a controversial point where it was discussed in the Imperial Parliament where it was eventually decided that an entire detachment of the IEC were to be sent to Smugglers Cove to remove the corrupt officials and restore order in the town. On an early spring morning this was launched with rapid pace, with hundreds of IEC making their moves in occupying strategic positions and arresting criminals and those from the rogue states. This was all well and good until a controversial arrest of a Raffordic merchant which eventually led to gunfire being shot at the IEC agents which caused a full scale battle in the town. It was brutal with around two thousand people being killed in the affair which led towards a full scale mobilisation and deployment of local militias, Imperial Guardsmen and the Military to be sent to protect the Empires northern borders. It then prompted a few decades long excursion of constant border incursions and conflicts leading to tens of thousands of the Empires soldiers and civilians being killed in the defense against the rogue states.

[b][u]Preparation & Mobilisation[/b][/u]
Eventually, these border conflicts went beyond the point of mild tolerance. Increasing ferocity of the rogue state, in particular the largest of them all, Raffordshire, had caused numerous issues that began to escalate to full on warfare and full battles comparable to ones you would see in proper official wars. Inevitably, the higher ups of the New Balion Empire decided that enough was enough and something had to be done. 

This border war along with the conflict with Daesun over Empire Island had caused the military budget to skyrocket to around a fifth of total government expenditure (around £180 Billion annually) and this also led to a rapid rise in the Royal Armys manpower which increased by over 100 thousand soldiers and rapid increase of the Militias and Imperial Guardsmen of the Dukelands, along with a rapidly expanding Air Force. This also led to new military bases and airfields being constructed at the Dukelands in preparation for a future conquest of the northern rogue Balionic states. As of the moment of announcement of new funding, there were in total around 11 Royal Army divisions, 23 local Militia divisions and 78 local Imperial Guardsmen brigades at the Dukelands, ready for an invasion.

However, no one had ever predicted that Raffordshire would launch one of the most evil bioweapons known to man. When Empire Islands communications had been ravaged, causing major disruptions around the Empire which included systems to check for diseases that had been put offline. In this chaotic window, a mysterious disease had appeared causing symptoms that havent been seen in over a hundred years to spread around Smugglers Cove and onto ships bound for Kianzhou. It then became apparent that it originated from secret biological labs deep in Raffordic territory and agents of the rogue states had infiltrated the borders and spread the disease now known as the Sarkos Virus. This immediately led to the IEC making strict checks closing down non-essential travel between settlements near the northern border and ensuring that the virus was under check, which to the delight of many, was done effectively and as soon as the Sarkos Virus appeared in the Empire, it quickly vanished thanks in part to an effective response by health officials and the IEC. The Raffordic agents that had spread the virus were caught drinking and fooling around at an informal brothel at Smugglers Cove by IEC agents and promptly executed in an alleyway, where the bodies were quickly disposed of. 

Despite the Sarkos Virus being effectively suppressed domestically, it eventually came to a decisive turning point where a conquest of the rogue Balionic states had to be done to ensure that those rebellious fools did not cause great international incident and damage. Deep at the headquarters of the Imperial Forces of New Balion, known famously as the Turquoise Citadel, plans were drawn up for an invasion, conquest and annexation of the rogue Balionic states with specific plans to crush the rogue armies, hold strategic positions and conduct a sweep of remaining rebels once the conquest had been successful. Plans were then secretly taken to the various civilian departments for an integration program so that the infrastructure, political and civil systems, energy, taxation and other elements of a functioning state were brought in to ensure an effective integration of the new provinces (made up of the former rogue states) into the rest of the Empire. New aristocratic and noble positions were organised and ready to be sprung into action once the conquest was effectively done and a major expansion of the Imperial Parliament was planned to ensure that the political system was extended for the new subjects of the Empire. It was also chosen from the already existing civil service and nobility in the rogue states, thanks in part by information from the Royal International Matters Bureau (RIMB), of whom would take current and new positions within the new provinces of the Empire. All in all, the plans for conquest were set. Now, it had to be sprung..
[/spoiler]
[spoiler=The Northern Conquests: Part 2 - The Invasion]
[b][u]Declaration of War[/b][/u]
On a cold, frosty Decembers morning it was then announced that what was known as Operation Northern Lightening was to sprung into action with a thumping announcement by His Majesty, Emperor Augustus X to the Imperial Parliament which all houses on this special occasion, had gathered at the traditional place for the state opening of each parliament session, the Gold Heraldly Chambers;

Ladies and gentlemen, pristine members of this loyal and faithful house, divinely ordained clergy, our bravest and most intelligent generals and all others of my loyal subjects gathered here today and listening at home, I have a major proclamation to make. As we are all aware, the rogue states that terrorized our northern communities for decades now have unleashed an evil virus upon us that was thankfully curtailed and the discovery to treat the virus was quick and swift enough. We have had enough. We will bring these evil cretins under control and with that I announce that on this day our brave soldiers will bring about that brave and virtuous task to bring our co-ethnic neighbours under ONE CROWN! 

This short but concise speech was received with genuine applause and celebration as the whole room stood up in standing ovation and cheering to signify their approval of the speech and the Empires conquest of the rogue states. Motions within parliament all showed unanimous approval of the Emperors speech and the invasion of the rogue states. On the streets major celebrations were held with crowds gathering around city and town centres all over the Empire (yes, even the besieged Empire Island) with crowds enthusiastic about the situation with chants of Long live the Emperor being sung in unison. Beer and other alcohol sales shot up as people were extremely happy and proud that at last, rogue Balionic states were beginning to be put under control. This vast public approval became even more apparent when massive numbers of young men showed up at recruiting stations across the Empire to sign up and fight for Emperor and Empire with around 150 thousand signing up for all branches of the military and tens of thousands applying for posts within the new provinces of the Empire. 

[b][u]Invasion & Grand Strategy[/b][/u]
As soon as the announcement had been made, the invasion began in quick notice. The invasion force was split up into 4 main army groups; Army Group 1 which dealt with the Western reaches of the rogue states which mainly had to deal with the mountainous and hilly conditions of the East Argos mountain which a large chunk of Rangehill had covered, Army Group 2 which went straight up north and covered the western half of the new border with [nation]Ascoiya[/nation] and primarily dealt with parts of Rangehill and Grockhill, Army Group 3 which also went northwards but covered the eastern half of the new border with Ascioya and also part of the sea border and primarily dealt with the largest and most evil state, Raffordshire and parts of Berimond, and finally Army Group 4 which went north-easternly and dealt with the remainder of Berimond and Eastcaster. All and all, these simple yet bold plans were deemed enough to deal with most of the rogue states. 

Imperial Air Force jets and bombers launched from their airbases and made swift strikes at the airfields and other air-related capable areas of the rogue states. It proved to be heavily effective as only a few jets of the rogue states were able to be deployed (and were quickly shot down) and their remaining air fields destroyed, with anti-air weaponry and equipment being ruthlessly hunted down and destroyed. This led to total air supremacy of the IAF and a plan was made by the various Air Marshalls of the Empire to cripple the rogue states ground capabilities. It was decided that major infrastructure such as vital factories would not be destroyed due to how valuable they would be after the conquest. Instead, bombings of various bridges, railways and other logistical places would be targeted and bombed. Another major place that was decided to be bombed was the largest rogue state city, Rafford. Rafford was obviously the central city of Raffordshire and was home to around 4.2 million people and was known as a sin city where all vices could be found and enjoyed for whoever seeks its pleasures. Once decisions were made, the bombing of those places with jets and missiles was conducted throughout the entire campaign. Ground troops were also targeted and in the later stages of the conquest, remaining pockets of resistance were bombed heavily until they surrendered or were destroyed. The bombing of Rafford city was effective, despite it being controversial as the city was devastated with bombs and missiles killing around 200 thousand civilians and making many more flee the city.

The Imperial Navy, despite its major focus being the dislodging of the Daesunian fleet off of Empire Island, was able to provide effective support for the ground forces along with blockading the coast of the rogue states. A fleet of 10 destroyers, 6 cruisers, 7 frigates, 2 escort carriers and dozens of other smaller vessels along with submarines were able to maintain a major blockade of the rogue states. Shipping coming in and out of the rogue states were intercepted and those ships were diverted towards ports within the Empire with anything valuable confiscated by the Imperial Navy and Marines and taken to the Empire to be exploited and utilised. Along with that, a few naval engagements occurred, mainly small scale skirmishes between smaller naval vessels. But one naval battle caused much more damage and notoriety. The largest combined fleet of the rogue states had managed to strike at the blockading ships at Point Roberts east of Eastcaster. One may think this was notable, however due to the lack of professionalism of the rogue state's navy it was ridiculously lopsided with jets from the escort carriers and missiles and guns from the rest of the ships making their hits, effectively crushing any chance of naval victory for the rogue states. In the end, the Imperial Navy added hundreds of new ships to its arsenal and easily found new crew from old naval personnel of the rogue states and new recruits.

Army Group 1, despite having difficult terrain to traverse and fight in, had the arguably the easiest time out of all of the army groups. It began moving towards their final objective lines within Rangehill which lay west and northwest of the Empires borders with rapid speed and had only a compartment of mainly local militia and Imperial Guardsmen due to their geographic location of the places of those units leading them to be trained effectively for mountain warfare. Due to this, the mountain rebels of Rangehill were surprised that their tactics against the invading Imperial forces were not working and were effectively crushed. Few native Argosi tribes that were present in the Rangehill territory that was now under the New Balion Empire were able to resist for slightly longer before detachments of the IEC were finally able to suppress them. Army Group 1 ended up taking the least casualties out of all of the Army Groups with only over three thousand dead and ten thousand wounded. It also became the first place where the new annexation procedures were implemented with infrastructure repaired and brought into the standards of the rest of the Empire and new systems and government administrations being put in place. Rockhill was now renamed the Westborders being led by the General, now Marquis Bernard Slim. 

Army Group 2 had not only had to deal with the northern borders of Rangehill and Grockham, but also reached and setting up the new border with Ascoiya. While it did not face the worst of the fighting, there was still heavy fighting. In particular was the Battle of Fort Costern where the Empire had to deal with stubborn resistance from the most elite units of Grockham. It did not help that there were several densely populated towns surrounding the Fort which led to extremely devastating urban combat which saw the towns being utterly destroyed with tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers of both sides being killed. In the end, Grockham (renamed Northham) had finally been annexed with the rare additional fact being that there was barely any resistance groups after occupation took place. 

Army Group 3 had the roughest time out of all the army groups. For starters, the main advance was through already rough and bitterly contested areas from the prior border which had heavy Raffordic presence which slowed down its advance and they had to contend with not only the heavily defended and potentially dangerous capture of the secret biological labs and the major cities, especially Rafford which still had millions of people within it. It had the largest invasion force with over 350 thousand soldiers and saw around 61 thousand casualties. Most of the casualties came from the capture of Rafford which was a brutal affair. Eventually the city was captured and the whole advance was made towards the border of Ascoiya and captured part of Berimond. The secret biological lab was eventually captured without major hassle and Imperial scientists were able to take control of the lab and find a cure to the Sarkos Virus.

Army Group 4 was able to smoothly move up the coast of the rogue states and was able to finally capture Eastcaster and the rest of Berimond. Although it was relatively smooth, they had to be greatly aided by naval bombardments and naval invasions by the Imperial Marines to flank and encircle many of the rogue troops. Eventually all of the rogue states had capitulated and surrendered to the New Balion Empire. In the end, the conquest cost around 52 thousand deaths from the Empire and around 189 thousand rogue state deaths. Many civilians were killed and displaced and the equipment (along with many willing former rogue state personal) being absorbed into the Imperial Military.
[/spoiler]
[spoiler=The Northern Conquests: Part 3 - The Aftermath]
After the conquest had formally ended, military parades were shown across the various towns and cities of the new conquests. Most notable being a parade in Rafford where a proclamation by the Emperor was read out by the new Duke of Raffordshire, Constan Herman to the wider populace of the 5 new provinces of the Empire;

Ladies and gentlemen of these new lands, you are not a foreign nation subjected by some random regime, you are now apart of your fellow coethnics grand, glorious Empire under the house of Augustus, of which I rule over you people. You will be grateful that we have been able to launch a reconquest of lands that were formerly part of the old Empire, meaning that as new subjects of the Empire, you will be part of the new system which will guarantee greater standard of living, a more prosperous economy and a lot more beneficial additions.. 

As the proclamation went on, parts of which were discussed were already being officiated, such as the reorganization of administrative districts, police forces, law systems and a bunch more. There would be 5 new provinces along with an additional £400-600 billion in GDP to the Empire. A further 58 million new subjects of the Empire would be added with noble titles already being established with around 65% of which were already pre-existing noble titles from the rogue states and the rest new ones to fill gaps from old rogue state nobles that refused to swear loyalty to the new Emperor they were under. Those who refused to acknowledge the new Emperor were quickly purged and those that resisted and/or had prior problems with the Empire were promptly arrested and jailed. The very worst of which, which included scientists that made the Sarkos Virus, were executed at haste. For the lowest chamber of parliament, the Commons Chamber of the Imperial Parliament, new elections were to be announced for the whole Empire which included the new provinces of the Empire. All in all, the integration process of the new provinces of the Empire was going smoothly and at pace and a new dawn for tens of millions was about to begin..
[/spoiler]

With the situation in Rosenmarkke and along the border undergoing radical shifts, concerns amongst the parties were raised regarding the push for unification, with most partymembers across the lines recognising that the secession of Knygta and Deyn was only the first of many.

It was thus, that on the evening of August 5 the heads of the various parties determined to meet at the home of Jean Luc Rousmonde for a discussion on what to do with the situation.

Thank you all for coming, stated Rousmonde, rising from his chair with a crystal glass in his hand, the other party heads nodded and raised their own glasses.

Now, as you know, the situation with which the king has dragged us into has led to a rapid collapse of the situation in Rosenmarkke, intoned Rousmonde, It is thus that I want us to consider the future, and where the hell this is all going,

Well, chairman, the general agreement amongst the members of my party, is that unification has become unavoidable at this point, I received word from a palace insider that Knygta and Deyn submitted their request to formally join Montfleur this morning, began Lilian Lucard.

The king will submit it to us no doubt, intoned Jacques Gusteau.

I doubt that, Jacque, it seems that the king has taken to his advisers and to the head of the government than to the party chambers, replied Rousmonde, Such a move shows that he may be preparing to sideline the parties in order to push through this unification process,

But unification is such a messy thing, interjected Rolande Perot, It would require vast referendums here in Montfleur, and place a massive burden on the state if not done well, I mean, look at the economy wed be inheriting, 

I do not disagree with that point, replied Gusteau, It is a risky move,

So we must take back the decision-making, replied Lucard.

Is there anything in the constitution? asked Gusteau.

We can issue a motion of censure, bar him from the chambers, replied Perot with a shrug.

The question is, would such a matter secure a vote majority? asked Rousemonde.

A good point, nodded Gusteau, As you may notice, compatriots, our right-wing friends are not here, and have made no effort to push back against the recent events, 

But they do not hold a majority, it should be no issue, replied Lucard.

They hold a slim majority, Lucard, two or three seats, replied Rousmonde.

Are there perhaps those who would oppose? The more moderate ones? asked Gusteau.

No, the moderates are too afraid of losing their seats in the next election, replied Perot.

The next election is soon is it not? asked Lucard.

It is in December, replied Rousmonde.

What are our polling positions looking like right now? asked Gusteau.

Well, unfortunately Li Baptistes are not doing so well in the polls, I would guess people are conflating us with the Strømmist ideology, began Rousmonde, The centrists, I believe they have  a lead no? he looked at Lucard and Gusteau.

Yes, the moderates are looking strong at this moment, but I do worry that might slide if this war begins to impact the economy, replied Lucard.

I doubt it will affect the economy, Rosenmarkke doesnt do or didnt do much major trade or business with us, beyond tourism, replied Gusteau.

So what are our options then, either we wrest the few right votes for a censure vote, or we wait for the elections? asked Perot.

We could petition the president, replied Gusteau, Request her to pass a war powers vote, 

Would a war powers vote work in stopping the king? asked Rousmonde.

It would potentially stall any motions to unite or accept any new regions without approval from the chamber, replied Lucard.

Then lets go with that, its mandated anyways, replied Gusteau.

I just worry about the votes, replied Rousmonde.

There is no need, it will be handled, replied Lucard, There are a few issues on the docket that the right need to have passed to secure a win in December.

Alright then, we shall do that, clapped Rousmonde, But if that fails, we will need to pivot to more drastic partywide motions, namely, strikes amongst the unions.

Strikes? asked Gusteau.

Yes, the king is not above the will of the people, and neither is the president, if the bourgeosie insist on acting like it is 1843 again, we shall treat them as such, replied Rousmonde sternly.[/quote]

In a meeting with Rosenmarkket collaborators and dissidents, particularly community leaders that had been worst affected by the bombing runs, the Count of Porcéan would agree that the best course of action for now to fill in the power vacuum left behind by the collapsing central government was to become the government himself. 

Shortly after 8 AM, the Count of Porcéan would formally proclaim the formation of the [i]Régence de La Rosemarche[/i] ("Regency of the Rose March"), a client state setup by Sallach to administer its interests in the region. Naturally, the Count of Porcéan would be established as its first regent, while several key institutions would also be created to give the Regency some veneer of legitimacy while the rest of the invasion had been proceeding along well.

A provisional Senate of Rosemarche would be created by decree, copied directly from the functions of the Senate of Sallach. This Senate would be staffed exclusively from Sallacher military officers and Rosenmarkket collaborators, and would be given two roles. First, the Economic Department, to be headed by a chief executive, who was to deal with all civilian functions of the new state such as taxation, transport, construction, and the continued operation of public services. Second, the Judicial Department, headed by a procurator, who functioned as the supreme court of the land in the absence of functioning judiciaries.

While the Count of Porcéan had initially hoped to fully copy the Sallacher senatorial system onto the new state, "logistical realities" would force him to carry out this simplified framework, and he would quickly make appointments to the chief executive and the procuratorate later in the day before departing for the frontlines to continue Operation Fusilier.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Battle of the Gardens[/b]][b]Battle of the Gardens[/b]

Initially, Sallacher forces had intended to storm the ducal palace to force the resignation of Antoine Jacques's government. Now, it had realized that the true objective was really to save that administration and to prevent the wider region from further falling into anarchy. 

The Count of Porcéan, bolstered by Montfleurois support and having been allowed to refuel and resupply undisturbed at the captured airfields, would continue its advance deeper into Bellegarde, hoping to reach the gardens of the ducal palace and force the final and total surrender of all Rosenmarkket forces in the area. 

Char 15 tanks roared deeply across the Belgardian countryside in the long approach to the ducal palace, while Sallacher reconnaissance teams and drone squads carefully navigated the dense hedges and forestry to guide the Count of Porcéan's columns away from soviet ambush. Meanwhile, the Sallacher Air Wing had succeeded in ferrying some 500 reinforcing gendarmes to support the invasion along with artillery and extra vehicles.

Assuming all goes well, the Count of Porcéan would be optimistic about total triumph in Belgarde within the week.[/spoiler][/quote]

[b]August 6, 2028: The Battle of Belgarde Begins[/b]

The main square of Wavre sat silent, the rubble of a collapsed building spilling out onto the square like a fainted woman. Cobblestones lay thrown about, and windows lay smashed open, their jagged remnants hanging in the windows, glinting in the morning light.

The bombing had caught the city off guard, forty-five citizens had found themselves dead or dying in the aftermath, twenty more died in the crush to escape the square. 

However, by the next morning, the bodies had been removed, and the street cleaners had worked overnight to scrub the bits of gore that clung to the cobblestone. Yet this did little to sweep away the silence that filled the once vibrant square.

In the history of a city there are times when silence is the greatest unifier for change, and sorrow the greatest engine for motion, and shock the greatest weapon against injustice. This was readily understood by the men and women of the XYZ foundation, who, met with haste following the bombing.

Gentlemen, declared Luc Rosseau, the leader of the foundation and a man of fine providence and well renown amongst the protestors, The armies of Sallach march upon us, they shall be here quicker than lightning, he had told the men, We must therefore not be broken up or cast around like sheep, but we must throng once more, he had declared between a glass of wine.

Truer words had not yet been spoken in the city, and truer words had not yet mobilised such a mass and a throng! 

It started with a cart, then a chair, then a table, rocks, bricks, stones themselves were pried from the ground and piled against the streets. Curious onlookers trudging past gave pause to see what was going on as the piles grew higher.

Indeed they were right to exist in a state of curiosity, for never before had such a raw assemblege of structure been constructed in the narrow streets of the city, yet up rose the barricades of the streets, as the citizens of the city, fueled by their rage and sorrow, made haste to begin the battle.

On the Rue Montremarte, the main road leading into the square, the pile had grown tall enough to reach the second floor and sat crooked and precarious in the street. Women hauled chairs from the restaurants and their homes, while two exchange students pushed and strained as they shoved a bureau into place. 

We need more support! shouted a voice from the top of the barricade, testing the strength of one of the sections as he waved at the two exchange students to help him lift a plank against the structure. 

Rousseau has ordered the city armory to be stormed at noon! He calls on all men to help! shouted another voice, a courier, who had run up to the barricade. 

The Armory? asked a woman nearby, who was ripping the nails out of a chair and placing them in a box filled with the objects. 

There is only one armory, laughed the courrier. 

The men groaned and strained as they continued to work, the sound of hammering filling the air. In other streets similar scenes played out, those closest to where soldiers or government officers could be present were more heavily armed, those farther away were generally calmer and slower in their pace. Supplies flowed only as long as they could be found, and for some, they had become harder to find as the larger barricades were fortified. 

As the sun rose higher in the sky, the government forces within the city had begun to mass at key strategic locations, recognisable by their blue and black uniforms these loyalists to the regime seemed nervous, as they appeared to casually stroll along the streets. 

Word had arrived that the Sallach forces had begun to make their approach to the city, unhindered by forces in the north as the soviets surrendered or were quickly forced into surrender. It was clear that these soldiers, citizens of Belgarde, were not as loyal to the regime had hoped.

For the citizens of Belgarde, it became clear that the government intended to put up a struggle, as word of a force from the Central Command in Mittlemarkke leaving the capital of Rosenmarkke in the south, reached the revolutionaries.

Belgarde now sat sandwiched between two forces, an untenable situation for the regional government, which now sat in the ducal palace, holed up as the city moved towards the precipice of revolt.

Antoine now sat at a small card table in the main sitting room of the palace, the curtains closed, and the dim light of the chandelier casting an eerie shade on the room as the provisional government of Belgarde discussed potential off-ramps for Belgarde.

The armies of the north are moving swiftly towards us, towns are reportedly greeting the Sallach and Montfleurois soldiers with applause and parades, began Antoine, looking at the feared faces of his compatriots.

We have reinforcements coming, from the capital, replied Peter Lor, the minister of finance for Belgarde.

Yes, but we do not know how many, intoned captain Raoul the head of the Belgarde SCSID and one of the few members of the pre-war SCSID that had survived.

And the city is about to enter into open revolt, there is no doubt that the revolutionaries intend to physically topple you from power, stated Lor nodding at Antoine.

Is it possible to negotiate? asked Antoine.

Raoul sucked in his breath, That would be treason, 

Yes, but what choice do we have? At least Sallach and the Montfleurois will treat us with kinder terms than the citizens of this city, declared Lor.

He has a point Raoul, you could get a nice house in the countryside, as opposed to a public hanging, nodded Antoine.

The situation is stressful right now, gentlemen, but not unsalvageable, the local police and forces will keep the citizens well off the government, and the back-up forces will ensure that we are well defended, replied Raoul.

How can you be so sure? demanded Antoine, How can you be so hopeful! he continued, striking the table with his open palm, missing the crystal glass that sat by his hand by mere inches. 

Because the current leadership is on the verge of collapse, the Council of 99 is allegedly going to meet in Knygta and Deyn, led by Josef Broz Østens to elect a new Chief Consul, replied Raoul.

And where did you hear of this? asked Lor.

An informant, someone close to Østens, he replied.

Antoine shook his head, Without confirmation of this, we must consider surrender, 

Raoul scoffed, And what? Have the new regime label us traitors? I can seek amnesty with Østens for us all,

No, you cannot, replied Antoine, Even if Østens somehow became Chief Consul, the world would demand Montfleur finish the job, 

So you are willing to give up? demanded Raoul.

If it means the stability of this region, yes, replied Antoine coldly.

Very well then, do so, but I will take no part of this, replied Raoul, rising from the table, Good day, he stated walking out of the room without another word.
